title: Bring regret under mercy, not despair
summary: Past actions cannot be edited away, and the future is not ours to command. Let regret become honest under Hukam instead of turning into a second punishment.
takeaway: Let the past be honest without letting it overrule Hukam.
lifeApplication: When an old mistake rises again, name it plainly and then stop bargaining with what cannot be rewritten. Ask what obedience to Hukam requires in the next step.

source.shortMeaning: Past actions are real, but the ego still does not control what comes next.
source.lifeApplication: When regret revisits, bring it under Hukam before it becomes self-punishment.

evidence.coreClaim: Past actions are real, but the ego still does not control what comes next.
evidence.turn: The shabad moves regret away from replay and into trust before the only Doer.
evidence.practicalImplication: When an old mistake rises again, name it plainly and then stop bargaining with what cannot be rewritten. Ask what obedience to Hukam requires in the next step.
